=== cell 5 markdown ===
So the region you measure on vsim (between `enter_vsim` and `exit_vsim`)
MUST be:

- M-mode only (no S-mode, no U-mode)
- No virtual memory / paging (satp is at reset = bare mode)
- Trap-free (no exceptions, no interrupts, no ebreak)
- PMP-static (no memory-protection setup is carried in)
- No semihosting (exception: the vplat runtime's MMIO-backed
  stdio / exit / file io is supported inside the ROI, see L1)
- No atomics that cross the handoff boundary
- No MMIO other than the vplat device set, UART2 + SimControl/HTIF (see L9)

If the measured region steps outside this envelope, the result is silently
wrong or the run hangs. Each case is listed below.

=== cell 6 markdown ===
## State coverage: what the wire format carries

Inventory view of the ROI rule above. Everything below is checked against
`include/hybrid/state_abi.h` (struct), the QEMU plugin drain
(`qemu_plugin/hybrid_handoff.c`), the vsim resume (`resume_driver.hpp`),
and the vsim drain (`state_drain.hpp`).

### Carried in `hybrid_state_v1`

- 32 GPRs, 32 FPRs
- `fcsr` (frm + sticky fflags; added 2026-06-12, closing L20)
- 13 M-mode CSRs: `mstatus, mepc, mtvec, mcause, mtval, mscratch,
  medeleg, mideleg, mip, mie, mcycle, minstret, satp`
- PMP: 16 `pmpcfg` + 64 `pmpaddr`
- V extension: `vstart, vtype, vl, vlenb, vreg[32], vxsat, vxrm, vcsr`
- F13 warmup metadata: `mcycle_at_measure_start`, `minstret_at_measure_start`
- `reserved[208]` = room for ~26 more `uint64` (wire format is version 2
  since L11 widened `vreg[]` to 128 bytes per register)

### NOT in the wire format at all

- All S-mode CSRs: `stvec, sepc, scause, stval, sscratch, sie, sip,
  scounteren, senvcfg, stimecmp`
- HPM block: `mhpmcounter3..31`, `mhpmevent3..31`, `mcounteren,
  menvcfg, mcountinhibit, mconfigptr, misa, time`
- Every Andes-custom CSR (`mmsc_cfg, mcache_ctl, mmisc_ctl, micm_cfg,
  mdcm_cfg, mxstatus, mdcause, mnvec`, ...). See L21.

### Carried but NOT restored into vsim

The QEMU1 plugin drains them into the struct, but `ResumeDriver`
writes none of them into the vsim hart. They are dead during the ROI:

- `satp` (L3), `mepc / mcause / mtval` (L4), `mscratch, medeleg,
  mideleg, mip, mie`, and all PMP (L2).

Only five CSRs are actually restored into vsim: `mstatus, mtvec,
mcycle, minstret, fcsr` (`resume_driver.hpp`).

### Transport ceiling - why "all CSRs" is not free

Three surfaces, three ceilings:

| Surface         | Mechanism                                     | Ceiling |
|-----------------|-----------------------------------------------|---------|
| QEMU1 drain     | plugin reads by NAME from gdbstub XML         | only CSRs the QEMU fork advertises |
| vsim resume     | DMI Abstract Cmd + Program Buffer (by number) | RO / WARL / locked bits will not take arbitrary values |
| vsim drain      | DMI Abstract read (by number)                 | general for any readable CSR |

Two structural blockers to "all CSRs":

1. Wire format is a fixed C struct; `reserved[208]` fits about 26 more
   `uint64`. Reaching the full M + S + HPM + Andes set needs a v2 layout.
2. Semantics, not just bits. Restore order and side effects already bite
   (`mstatus.FS/VS` gating, `vsetvl` atomicity for `vtype/vl`). Writing
   `satp` flushes the TLB; Andes `mcache_ctl / mmisc_ctl` toggle caches,
   prefetchers, branch prediction and may be RO or locked when written
   via the debug module mid-run. Those are exactly the CSRs that shape
   the cycle figure.

Verdict: extending the wire format to a bounded set in this way is
feasible - the L20 fix is the worked example (one `uint64` carved from
`reserved[]`, drained by name, restored via the existing
abstract-or-PB write, read back at drain). S-mode t

## Tier 2 - Will break when you scale up

### L6. Whole-program (S/U-mode) privilege is forced to M-mode  (F-T2.1)

- When it bites: a kernel/Linux-style workload that is in S- or U-mode at
  the trigger boundary.
- What happens: both sides hardcode `priv = 3` (M-mode):
  `state_drain.hpp:53` and `hybrid_handoff.c:314`. On the vsim side
  DCSR.prv is never written, so `dret` always resumes in M-mode. S/U code
  then raises illegal-instruction -> trap loop.
- Where: `state_drain.hpp:53`, `hybrid_handoff.c:314`.
- Status: OPEN.

The hardcode is one line on each side of the handoff:

The `verilator/tests/hybrid/*.test.cpp` doctest unit tests are header-only
(C++20 + ABI header) and run directly on the host - no podman/Verilator needed.
Build+run one with:

```sh
cd /home/nick/work/hybrid_sim
g++ -std=c++20 -I verilator/src -I verilator/tests/hybrid -I include \
    -I verilator/external/doctest/doctest \
    verilator/tests/hybrid/resume_driver.test.cpp -o /tmp/t && /tmp/t
```

`-I verilator/tests/hybrid` is only needed for tests that include the shared
`recording_bus.hpp` (e.g. state_drain). This is the fast RED/GREEN loop; the
canonical container/ctest path is only required for the e2e suite.

Exceptions that do NOT link on the host: `qemu_handback.test.cpp` (needs libfmt:
`undefined reference to fmt::v11::...`), and the SystemC-dependent ones
(`*_smoke.cpp`, `shared_mem_offset.test.cpp`). Skip those on host.

vsim rebuild after editing `src/hybrid/*.hpp` or `src/simulator.hpp`:
`bash scripts/build_vsim.sh` (podman; incremental, recompiles `main.cpp.o` only,
RTL is cached - ~30s). Then e2e: `JOBS=8 FILTER=rt_c_v bash scripts/run_e2e.sh`.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# End-to-end harness: QEMU 1 + plugin -> vsim (2-phase, no QEMU2 handback).
#
# Memory between QEMU and vsim is shared via an /dev/shm-backed mmap
# (128 MB). Works for both asm fixtures (handoff_roundtrip, rt_*) and
# C-level fixtures (rt_c_*). C fixtures require shared mmap so the
# stack/heap survives handoffs; asm fixtures don't need it but run
# fine with it.
#
# Env:
#   FIXTURE         REQUIRED. .elf name under tests/fixtures/ (no .elf suffix).
#   TRIGGER_MODE    marker | pc (default marker).
#   ROI_START       pc mode switch-in PC: a 0x address or a symbol in
#                   $VSIM_ELF. If BOTH ROI_START and ROI_END are unset, they
#                   are auto-derived from the fixture's ROI marker HINTs via
#                   objdump (see roi_markers_from_disasm) -- the bulk runner
#                   relies on this; ./andes-sim run always passes them explicitly.
#   ROI_END         pc mode switch-out PC, same forms / same auto-derivation.
#   TIMEOUT         vsim leg timeout in seconds (default 60).
#   VERIFY=1        opt-in differential verification (default off): re-run
#                   the ELF on pure QEMU with the plugin draining at the ROI
#                   exit boundary (the oracle), then `andes-sim state-diff`
#                   the oracle state against the vsim drain. Any divergence
#                   in what vsim freshly drains (pc/GPRs/FPRs/V) fails the
#                   test; counters and passthrough CSRs are excluded.
#   CHECK_MCYCLE_MONOTONIC=1   assert mcycle/minstret strictly increased
#                              between QEMU 1's drain and vsim's drain.
#   WARMUP_ICOUNT              gem5-style warmup window. When set and > 0,
#                              passes --vsim-warmup-icount K to vsim and
#                              prints a [warmup] line carrying the captured
#                              (mcycle_at_measure_start, minstret_at_measure_start)
#                              pair from the drained state file.
#   VSIM_BIN, VSIM_QEMU, VSIM_PLUGIN, VSIM_ELF, NM  override built paths.

set -euo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/lib/paths.sh"
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/lib/roi.sh"

FIXTURE="${FIXTURE:?FIXTURE env var is required (e.g. FIXTURE=rt_c_hello)}"
TIMEOUT="${TIMEOUT:-60}"
TRIGGER_MODE="${TRIGGER_MODE:-marker}"

hybrid_resolve_paths

NM="${NM:-${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:+$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-nm}}"
NM="${NM:-riscv64-unknown-elf-nm}"

case "$TRIGGER_MODE" in
  marker) ;;
  pc)
    if ! command -v "$NM" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
      echo "skip[$FIXTURE pc]: nm not found at $NM"
      exit 77
    fi
    # ROI_START / ROI_END name the two switch PCs (0x address or symbol in
    # $VSIM_ELF). ./andes-sim run always passes them explicitly. When a caller
    # leaves BOTH unset (e.g. the bulk runner scripts/run_e2e.sh), derive them
    # from the fixture's ROI marker HINTs via objdump, so pc mode needs no
    # per-fixture config and no planted boundary symbols. A partial set or a
    # derivation miss falls through to roi_resolve_pair's required-vars error.
    if [ -z "${ROI_START:-}" ] && [ -z "${ROI_END:-}" ]; then
      OBJDUMP="${OBJDUMP:-${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:+$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-objdump}}"
      OBJDUMP="${OBJDUMP:-riscv64-unknown-elf-objdump}"
      if command -v "$OBJDUMP" >/dev/null 2>&1 \
         && MARKERS=$(roi_markers_from_disasm "$("$OBJDUMP" -d "$VSIM_ELF")"); then
        ROI_START="0x${MARKERS%% *}"
        ROI_END="0x${MARKERS##* }"
        export ROI_START ROI_END
      fi
    fi
    NM_OUT=$("$NM" --defined-only "$VSIM_ELF")
    roi_resolve_pair "$NM_OUT" "$FIXTURE pc" || exit 1
    ;;
  *)
    echo "FAIL[$FIXTURE]: unknown TRIGGER_MODE=$TRIGGER_MODE (use marker|pc)"
    exit 1
    ;;
esac

# 128 MB matches the QEMU virt machine default; vsim uses the same size.
SHARED_SIZE=$((128 * 1024 * 1024))
SHARED_MEM=$(mktemp -p /dev/shm vsim-e2e-shared.XXXXXX)
STATE_QEMU=$(mktemp)
STATE_VSIM=$(mktemp)
STATE_ORACLE=$(mktemp)
SIM_LOG=$(mktemp)
trap 'rm -f "$SHARED_MEM" "$STATE_QEMU" "$STATE_VSIM" "$STATE_ORACLE" "$SIM_LOG"' EXIT
truncate -s "$SHARED_SIZE" "$SHARED_MEM"

PLUGIN_ARGS="outfile=$STATE_QEMU"
VSIM_TRIG_ARGS=()
if [ "$TRIGGER_MODE" = "pc" ]; then
  PLUGIN_ARGS="$PLUGIN_ARGS,enter_pc=0x$ENTER_PC"
  VSIM_TRIG_ARGS=(--hybrid-exit-pc "0x$EXIT_PC")
fi

# F21: forward --vsim-warmup-icount when caller asked for a warmup window.
VSIM_WARMUP_ARGS=()
if [ "${WARMUP_ICOUNT:-0}" -gt 0 ] 2>/dev/null; then
  VSIM_WARMUP_ARGS=(--vsim-warmup-icount "$WARMUP_ICOUNT")
fi

# Optional ROI kanata logging: hsim sets KANATA_FILE (and optionally
# OBJDUMP_FILE) when the user passes --kanata. vsim's --kanata-roi auto-
# derives the window from the resume PC and the unique exit PC.
VSIM_KANATA_ARGS=()
if [ -n "${KANATA_FILE:-}" ]; then
  VSIM_KANATA_ARGS+=(--kanata "$KANATA_FILE" --kanata-roi)
  if [ -n "${OBJDUMP_FILE:-}" ]; then
    VSIM_KANATA_ARGS+=(--objdump "$OBJDUMP_FILE")
  fi
fi

echo "[$FIXTURE 1/2 mode=$TRIGGER_MODE] QEMU 1: drain entry state"
set +e
"$VSIM_QEMU" \
  -object "memory-backend-file,id=mem,share=on,mem-path=$SHARED_MEM,size=$SHARED_SIZE" \
  -machine andes_ae350,memory-backend=mem \

# End-to-end harness: QEMU 1 + plugin -> vsim (2-phase, no QEMU2 handback).
#
# Memory between QEMU and vsim is shared via an /dev/shm-backed mmap
# (128 MB). Works for both asm fixtures (handoff_roundtrip, rt_*) and
# C-level fixtures (rt_c_*). C fixtures require shared mmap so the
# stack/heap survives handoffs; asm fixtures don't need it but run
# fine with it.
#
# Env:
#   FIXTURE         REQUIRED. .elf name under tests/fixtures/ (no .elf suffix).
#   TRIGGER_MODE    marker | pc (default marker).
#   ROI_START       pc mode switch-in PC: a 0x address or a symbol in
#                   $VSIM_ELF. If BOTH ROI_START and ROI_END are unset, they
#                   are auto-derived from the fixture's ROI marker HINTs via
#                   objdump (see roi_markers_from_disasm) -- the bulk runner
#                   relies on this; ./andes-sim run always passes them explicitly.
#   ROI_END         pc mode switch-out PC, same forms / same auto-derivation.
#   TIMEOUT         vsim leg timeout in seconds (default 60).
#   VERIFY=1        opt-in differential verification (default off): re-run
#                   the ELF on pure QEMU with the plugin draining at the ROI
#                   exit boundary (the oracle), then `andes-sim state-diff`
#                   the oracle state against the vsim drain. Any divergence
#                   in what vsim freshly drains (pc/GPRs/FPRs/V) fails the
#                   test; counters and passthrough CSRs are excluded.
#   CHECK_MCYCLE_MONOTONIC=1   assert mcycle/minstret strictly increased
#                              between QEMU 1's drain and vsim's drain.
#   WARMUP_ICOUNT              gem5-style warmup window. When set and > 0,
#                              passes --vsim-warmup-icount K to vsim and
#                              prints a [warmup] line carrying the captured
#                              (mcycle_at_measure_start, minstret_at_measure_start)
#                              pair from the drained state file.
#   VSIM_BIN, VSIM_QEMU, VSIM_PLUGIN, VSIM_ELF, NM  override built paths.

set -euo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/lib/paths.sh"
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/lib/roi.sh"

FIXTURE="${FIXTURE:?FIXTURE env var is required (e.g. FIXTURE=rt_c_hello)}"
TIMEOUT="${TIMEOUT:-60}"
TRIGGER_MODE="${TRIGGER_MODE:-marker}"

hybrid_resolve_paths

NM="${NM:-${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:+$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-nm}}"
NM="${NM:-riscv64-unknown-elf-nm}"

case "$TRIGGER_MODE" in
  marker) ;;
  pc)
    if ! command -v "$NM" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
      echo "skip[$FIXTURE pc]: nm not found at $NM"
      exit 77
    fi
    # ROI_START / ROI_END name the two switch PCs (0x address or symbol in
    # $VSIM_ELF). ./andes-sim run always passes them explicitly. When a caller
    # leaves BOTH unset (e.g. the bulk runner scripts/run_e2e.sh), derive them
    # from the fixture's ROI marker HINTs via objdump, so pc mode needs no
    # per-fixture config and no planted boundary symbols. A partial set or a
    # derivation miss falls through to roi_resolve_pair's required-vars error.
    if [ -z "${ROI_START:-}" ] && [ -z "${ROI_END:-}" ]; then
      OBJDUMP="${OBJDUMP:-${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:+$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-objdump}}"
      OBJDUMP="${OBJDUMP:-riscv64-unknown-elf-objdump}"
      if command -v "$OBJDUMP" >/dev/null 2>&1 \
         && MARKERS=$(roi_markers_from_disasm "$("$OBJDUMP" -d "$VSIM_ELF")"); then
        ROI_START="0x${MARKERS%% *}"
        ROI_END="0x${MARKERS##* }"
        export ROI_START ROI_END
      fi
    fi
    NM_OUT=$("$NM" --defined-only "$VSIM_ELF")
    roi_resolve_pair "$NM_OUT" "$FIXTURE pc" || exit 1
    ;;
  *)
    echo "FAIL[$FIXTURE]: unknown TRIGGER_MODE=$TRIGGER_MODE (use marker|pc)"
    exit 1
    ;;
esac

# 128 MB matches the QEMU virt machine default; vsim uses the same size.
SHARED_SIZE=$((128 * 1024 * 1024))
SHARED_MEM=$(mktemp -p /dev/shm vsim-e2e-shared.XXXXXX)
STATE_QEMU=$(mktemp)
STATE_VSIM=$(mktemp)
STATE_ORACLE=$(mktemp)
SIM_LOG=$(mktemp)
trap 'rm -f "$SHARED_MEM" "$STATE_QEMU" "$STATE_VSIM" "$STATE_ORACLE" "$SIM_LOG"' EXIT
truncate -s "$SHARED_SIZE" "$SHARED_MEM"

PLUGIN_ARGS="outfile=$STATE_QEMU"
VSIM_TRIG_ARGS=()
if [ "$TRIGGER_MODE" = "pc" ]; then
  PLUGIN_ARGS="$PLUGIN_ARGS,enter_pc=0x$ENTER_PC"
  VSIM_TRIG_ARGS=(--hybrid-exit-pc "0x$EXIT_PC")
fi

# F21: forward --vsim-warmup-icount when caller asked for a warmup window.
VSIM_WARMUP_ARGS=()
if [ "${WARMUP_ICOUNT:-0}" -gt 0 ] 2>/dev/null; then
  VSIM_WARMUP_ARGS=(--vsim-warmup-icount "$WARMUP_ICOUNT")
fi

# Optional ROI kanata logging: hsim sets KANATA_FILE (and optionally
# OBJDUMP_FILE) when the user passes --kanata. vsim's --kanata-roi auto-
# derives the window from the resume PC and the unique exit PC.
VSIM_KANATA_ARGS=()
if [ -n "${KANATA_FILE:-}" ]; then
  VSIM_KANATA_ARGS+=(--kanata "$KANATA_FILE" --kanata-roi)
  if [ -n "${OBJDUMP_FILE:-}" ]; then
    VSIM_KANATA_ARGS+=(--objdump "$OBJDUMP_FILE")
  fi
fi

echo "[$FIXTURE 1/2 mode=$TRIGGER_MODE] QEMU 1: drain entry state"
set +e
"$VSIM_QEMU" \
  -object "memory-backend-file,id=mem,share=on,mem-path=$SHARED_MEM,size=$SHARED_SIZE" \
  -machine andes_ae350,memory-backend=mem \

-machine andes_ae350,memory-backend=mem \
  -cpu andes-ax45mpv,vlen=512 \
  -nographic \
  -semihosting-config enable=on,target=native \
  -bios "$VSIM_ELF" \
  -plugin "$VSIM_PLUGIN,$PLUGIN_ARGS" </dev/null >/dev/null 2>&1
QEMU1_RC=$?
set -e

if [ "$QEMU1_RC" -ne 200 ]; then
  echo "FAIL[$FIXTURE]: QEMU 1 expected exit 200 on drain, got $QEMU1_RC"
  exit 1
fi

if [ ! -s "$STATE_QEMU" ]; then
  echo "FAIL[$FIXTURE]: QEMU 1 did not produce state"
  exit 1
fi

echo "[$FIXTURE 2/2 mode=$TRIGGER_MODE] vsim: resume + drain"
set +e
timeout "$TIMEOUT" "$VSIM_BIN" "$VSIM_ELF" \
  --resume-from-qemu "$STATE_QEMU" \
  --handoff-out "$STATE_VSIM" \
  --shared-mem-path "$SHARED_MEM" \
  --shared-mem-size "$SHARED_SIZE" \
  --shared-mem-base 0x00000000 \
  "${VSIM_TRIG_ARGS[@]}" \
  "${VSIM_KANATA_ARGS[@]}" \
  "${VSIM_WARMUP_ARGS[@]}" </dev/null >"$SIM_LOG" 2>&1
VSIM_RC=$?
set -e

# vsim drained on the exit trigger and exited 200 (kExitHandoffToQemu).
# Anything else is a hard failure: the cycle figure is only valid when vsim
# drained cleanly.
if [ "$VSIM_RC" -ne 200 ]; then
  echo "FAIL[$FIXTURE]: vsim expected exit 200 (drain), got $VSIM_RC"
  echo "--- sim log ---"
  cat "$SIM_LOG"
  exit 1
fi

# Kernel cycles (always) + opt-in monotonic check. Offsets locked by
# state_abi_check.h (mcycle@624, minstret@632). vsim restores mcycle from
# QEMU 1's drain then counts real clock cycles, so vsim_mcycle - qemu1_mcycle
# is the measured region's cycle count. Runs before the RC gate so the
# verdict is independent of any downstream-phase failure.
read_u64_le() { od -A n -j "$1" -N 8 -t u8 "$2" | tr -d ' \n'; }
if [ -s "$STATE_VSIM" ] && [ -s "$STATE_QEMU" ]; then
  Q1_MCYCLE=$(read_u64_le 624 "$STATE_QEMU")
  Q1_MINST=$(read_u64_le  632 "$STATE_QEMU")
  V_MCYCLE=$(read_u64_le  624 "$STATE_VSIM")
  V_MINST=$(read_u64_le   632 "$STATE_VSIM")
  echo "[$FIXTURE kernel_cycles] $((V_MCYCLE - Q1_MCYCLE))  (vsim mcycle=$V_MCYCLE - qemu1 mcycle=$Q1_MCYCLE)"
  # F21: when WARMUP_ICOUNT is set, surface the snapshot pair so callers
  # can verify the warmup window without re-parsing the state file.
  # Offsets locked by include/hybrid/state_abi_check.h (F13, ceiling 128):
  #   mcycle_at_measure_start@5440, minstret_at_measure_start@5448.
  if [ "${WARMUP_ICOUNT:-0}" -gt 0 ] 2>/dev/null; then
    MS_MC=$(read_u64_le 5440 "$STATE_VSIM")
    MS_MI=$(read_u64_le 5448 "$STATE_VSIM")
    echo "[$FIXTURE warmup] K=$WARMUP_ICOUNT mcycle_at_measure_start=$MS_MC minstret_at_measure_start=$MS_MI"
  fi
  if [ "${CHECK_MCYCLE_MONOTONIC:-0}" = "1" ]; then
    echo "[$FIXTURE mcycle/minstret] qemu1: mcycle=$Q1_MCYCLE minstret=$Q1_MINST"
    echo "[$FIXTURE mcycle/minstret] vsim:  mcycle=$V_MCYCLE minstret=$V_MINST"
    if [ "$V_MCYCLE" -le "$Q1_MCYCLE" ]; then
      echo "FAIL[$FIXTURE]: mcycle not strictly increasing across vsim"
      exit 1
    fi
    if [ "$V_MINST" -le "$Q1_MINST" ]; then
      echo "FAIL[$FIXTURE]: minstret not strictly increasing across vsim"
      exit 1
    fi
    echo "[$FIXTURE mcycle/minstret] PASS: strictly increasing"
  fi
fi

# verify_oracle F3 (opt-in, default off): differential check against a
# pure-QEMU oracle. The same ELF re-runs on QEMU alone -- clean memory, so
# NO shared mmap (reusing it would leak the hybrid run's post-ROI bytes
# into the oracle's boot) -- with the plugin draining at the ROI exit
# boundary. state-diff then compares everything vsim freshly drains.
if [ "${VERIFY:-0}" = "1" ]; then
  ANDES_SIM_BIN="${ANDES_SIM_BIN:-$TOP_ROOT/build/andes-sim}"
  if [ ! -x "$ANDES_SIM_BIN" ]; then
    echo "FAIL[$FIXTURE]: VERIFY=1 needs $ANDES_SIM_BIN (run scripts/build_driver.sh)"
    exit 1
  fi
  ORACLE_TRIG="exit_marker=1"
  [ "$TRIGGER_MODE" = "pc" ] && ORACLE_TRIG="exit_pc=0x$EXIT_PC"
  # Sample at vsim's ACTUAL halt point: the DMI halt lands a variable 0-3
  # insns past the trigger, so the oracle must drain at the pc vsim's state
  # file reports (offset 16, locked by state_abi_check.h), not at trigger+1.
  VSIM_PC=$(printf '0x%x' "$(read_u64_le 16 "$STATE_VSIM")")
  ORACLE_TRIG="$ORACLE_TRIG,drain_pc=$VSIM_PC"

  echo "[$FIXTURE verify mode=$TRIGGER_MODE] oracle: pure QEMU drains at ROI exit (pc=$VSIM_PC)"
  set +e
  "$VSIM_QEMU" \
    -machine andes_ae350 \
    -cpu andes-ax45mpv,vlen=512 \
    -nographic \
    -semihosting-config enable=on,target=native \
    -bios "$VSIM_ELF" \
    -plugin "$VSIM_PLUGIN,outfile=$STATE_ORACLE,$ORACLE_TRIG" \
    </dev/null >/dev/null 2>&1
  ORACLE_RC=$?
  set -e
  if [ "$ORACLE_RC" -ne 200 ]; then
    echo "FAIL[$FIXTURE]: oracle QEMU expected exit 200 on drain, got $ORACLE_RC"
    exit 1
  fi

  set +e
  DIFF_OUT=$("$ANDES_SIM_BIN" state-diff "$STATE_ORACLE" "$STATE_VSIM" 2>&1)
  DIFF_RC=$?
  set -e
  printf '%s\n' "$DIFF_OUT"
  if [ "$DIFF_RC" -ne 0 ]; then
    echo "FAIL[$FIXTURE]: vsim drain diverges from the QEMU oracle"
    exit 1
  fi
  echo "[$FIXTURE verify] PASS: vsim drain matches the QEMU oracle"
fi

echo "[$FIXTURE PASS] 2-phase handoff complete (QEMU 1 drain -> vsim drain)"

}
require VSIM_QEMU   "$VSIM_QEMU"
require VSIM_PLUGIN "$VSIM_PLUGIN"
require VSIM_BIN    "$VSIM_BIN"

export VSIM_QEMU VSIM_PLUGIN VSIM_BIN

REQUIRED_ELFS=(
  handoff_roundtrip rt_pc_jump rt_sign_bits rt_abi_aliases rt_long_roi
  rt_all_gprs rt_mem_loadstore rt_unaligned_lh rt_csr_survival rt_shared_mem
  rt_c_hello rt_c_printf rt_c_matmul rt_c_fcsr rt_c_v_regs rt_c_v_csrs
  rt_c_v_matmul rt_c_v_fill
  # CSR-less spin loop; used by `./andes-sim run --mode icount` and the BBV-emit
  # / SimPoint stages.
  icount_spin
)
need_build=0
for f in "${REQUIRED_ELFS[@]}"; do
  [[ -e "$TEST_DIR/$f.elf" ]] || need_build=1
done
if (( need_build )); then
  step "building test ELFs in $TEST_DIR"

# Build tiny RV64 fixtures used by hybrid smoke tests.
#
# Toolchain location comes from the repo-root config.env (loaded by
# `source ./setup.sh`, which exports HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN). Override on the
# command line with `make TOOLCHAIN=/path/to/toolchain ...` if you want
# to bypass the env var.

TOOLCHAIN ?= $(HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN)
ifeq ($(strip $(TOOLCHAIN)),)
$(error HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN is not set. Run `source ./setup.sh` from the repo root, or pass `TOOLCHAIN=/path/to/toolchain` on the command line)
endif
CC        := $(TOOLCHAIN)/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-gcc
LD        := $(TOOLCHAIN)/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-ld
OBJDUMP   := $(TOOLCHAIN)/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-objdump

# Runtime sources live at the repo root (runtime/) -- they are the
# user-facing andes-sim runtime; fixtures are just one consumer. The linker
# script moved with them (test.ld -> runtime/andes-sim.ld, same content).
RUNTIME_DIR := ../../runtime
LDSCRIPT    := $(RUNTIME_DIR)/andes-sim.ld
# Fixture-only helpers (csr ROI markers; NOT part of the portable runtime).
HELPERS_DIR := runtime

CFLAGS  := -march=rv64gc -mabi=lp64d -nostdlib -static -Wall
LDFLAGS := -T $(LDSCRIPT) -nostdlib -static

# All fixtures share andes-sim.ld (load base 0x00100000, andes_ae350 DRAM).
RT_FIXTURES := rt_all_gprs rt_abi_aliases rt_sign_bits rt_pc_jump \
               rt_long_roi rt_mem_loadstore rt_unaligned_lh \
               rt_shared_mem rt_csr_survival

# C-level fixtures: standard newlib stdio (printf, fputs, ...) linked
# through the shipped vplat runtime (libandes_sim_runtime.a) with the
# same two-flag command users type (-B build/runtime
# -specs=andes-sim.specs), so the suites regression-test the real
# artifact. stdio goes out the ATCUART100 UART2 and exit/file-io through
# the SimControl device at 0xe0080000, all of which both QEMU's
# andes_ae350 and vsim model. No semihosting and no libgloss anywhere:
# vplat_syscalls.o in the archive provides every stub newlib needs, so
# the same ELF runs on fast, cycle AND hybrid and a syscall inside the
# ROI works (it just adds its real cycles to the figure).

                    rt_c_no_trigger_exit rt_c_fcsr
RT_C_V_FIXTURES  := rt_c_v_regs rt_c_v_csrs rt_c_v_matmul rt_c_v_fill
RT_C_VPLAT_FIXTURES := vplat_hello vplat_exit41 vplat_file

VPLAT_RT_DIR := ../../build/runtime
VPLAT_RT     := $(VPLAT_RT_DIR)/libandes_sim_runtime.a $(VPLAT_RT_DIR)/crt0.o \

# link cleanly into rv64gcv programs (ld unions the arch attributes).
# The crt0 already sets mstatus.VS to Initial, so V insns don't trap.
VPLAT_V_CFLAGS := -march=rv64gcv -mabi=lp64d -O1 -Wall

# Note: handoff.elf, handoff_exit.elf, spin.elf are referenced only by the
# EXCLUDE_FROM_ALL handoff_smoke.cpp target; they still build here for
# completeness. All targets share andes-sim.ld at 0x00100000.

spin.elf: spin.S $(LDSCRIPT)
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c spin.S -o spin.o
	$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) spin.o -o $@

# CSR-less spin for F5 plugin-icount e2e. Linked at 0x00100000 (andes-sim.ld)
# so andes_ae350's MROM at 0x80000000 stays clear when loaded via -bios.
icount_spin.elf: icount_spin.S $(LDSCRIPT)
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c icount_spin.S -o icount_spin.o
	$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) icount_spin.o -o $@

handoff.elf: handoff.S $(LDSCRIPT)
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c handoff.S -o handoff.o
	$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) handoff.o -o $@

handoff_exit.elf: handoff_exit.S $(LDSCRIPT)
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c handoff_exit.S -o handoff_exit.o
	$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) handoff_exit.o -o $@

handoff_roundtrip.elf: handoff_roundtrip.S $(LDSCRIPT) semihost_exit.inc
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c handoff_roundtrip.S -o handoff_roundtrip.o
	$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) handoff_roundtrip.o -o $@

$(RT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf): %.elf: %.S $(LDSCRIPT) semihost_exit.inc
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c $< -o $*.o
	$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) $*.o -o $@

# C-level fixtures: linked exactly like a user program (see VPLAT_RT
# above). rt_c_helpers.h rides -I$(HELPERS_DIR).
$(RT_C_FIXTURES:%=%.elf): %.elf: %.c $(VPLAT_RT) $(HELPERS_DIR)/rt_c_helpers.h
	$(CC) $(VPLAT_CFLAGS) -I$(HELPERS_DIR) \
	  -B $(VPLAT_RT_DIR) -specs=andes-sim.specs $< -o $@

# RVV-enabled fixtures: same link, different -march. Listed separately so
# changes to VPLAT_CFLAGS don't accidentally drop V.
$(RT_C_V_FIXTURES:%=%.elf): %.elf: %.c $(VPLAT_RT) $(HELPERS_DIR)/rt_c_helpers.h
	$(CC) $(VPLAT_V_CFLAGS) -I$(HELPERS_DIR) \
	  -B $(VPLAT_RT_DIR) -specs=andes-sim.specs $< -o $@

# vplat smoke fixtures (tests/vplat/): exercise the runtime's own
# features (exit code, file io) with no fixture helpers.
$(RT_C_VPLAT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf): %.elf: %.c $(VPLAT_RT)
	$(CC) $(VPLAT_CFLAGS) -B $(VPLAT_RT_DIR) -specs=andes-sim.specs $< -o $@

# One sub-make produces all five artifacts (grouped target, make >= 4.3).
$(VPLAT_RT) &: $(RUNTIME_SRCS) $(RUNTIME_DIR)/vplat_syscalls.c \
               $(RUNTIME_DIR)/andes-sim.ld $(RUNTIME_DIR)/andes-sim.specs \
               $(RUNTIME_DIR)/roi.h
	$(MAKE) -C $(RUNTIME_DIR)

# Markerless GEMM twin (gemm_modes.md F2). Explicit rule, NOT in

rt_c_v_matmul_free.elf: rt_c_v_matmul.c $(VPLAT_RT) $(HELPERS_DIR)/rt_c_helpers.h

	  -B $(VPLAT_RT_DIR) -specs=andes-sim.specs rt_c_v_matmul.c -o $@

	$(OBJDUMP) -d handoff_exit.elf

# priv_modes -- resolve L6: S/U-mode privilege across the handoff

Goal: a trap-free, paging-off ROI that sits in S- or U-mode at the
trigger boundary measures correctly. Today both drain sites hardcode
`priv = 3` and vsim never writes `dcsr.prv`, so `dret` always resumes
in M-mode (L6).

Input:  an ELF whose ROI runs in S- or U-mode (entered via `mret`
        before the ENTER marker, PMP opened in the M-mode preamble).
Output: `hybrid_state_v1::priv` carries the real privilege on both
        drains, vsim executes the ROI in that privilege, and the
        kernel-cycle figure is valid. `CHECK_PRIV=<0|1|3>` in
        tests/e2e.sh asserts it.

Scope notes:
- PMP restore rides along (gated on priv != M): with PMP implemented
  and no matching entry, every S/U access faults -- an S/U ROI cannot
  even fetch on the vsim side without the producer's PMP block. This
  moves L2 from open to partial.
- NOT in scope: S-mode CSR transport (stvec/sepc/sscratch/satp...).
  Those are consulted on traps and paging, which the ROI envelope
  already forbids (L3/L4). An S/U ROI that READS them sees vsim reset
  values -- documented limitation.

// rt_priv_umode.S
//
// L6 fixture: the ROI runs in U-mode. Same shape as rt_priv_smode.S
// (see there for the why of each step); only the mret target privilege
// differs -- MPP stays U (00) -- and the harness expects CHECK_PRIV=0.

#include "semihost_exit.inc"

.section .text
.globl _start
_start:
    li      t0, -1
    csrw    pmpaddr0, t0            // NAPOT over the full address space
    li      t0, 0x1F                // A=NAPOT | X | W | R
    csrw    pmpcfg0, t0

    la      t0, trap_exit
    csrw    mtvec, t0

    li      t0, (3 << 11)
    csrc    mstatus, t0             // MPP <- U (00)
    la      t0, roi
    csrw    mepc, t0
    mret                            // drop to U-mode

roi:
    slti    x0, x0, 0x5A0           // ENTER: QEMU1 drains, priv must be 0

    li      t1, 0x7000
    li      t2, 53
    mul     t3, t1, t2              // U-mode work; lands in the drained GPRs

    slti    x0, x0, 0x5A1           // EXIT: vsim drains, priv must be 0
    nop                             // halt slack: the DMI halt lands 0-3
    nop                             // insns past the trigger; keep the
    nop                             // privilege-changing ecall out of its
    nop                             // reach so the drained prv stays U
    ecall                           // U -> M (medeleg=0): trap_exit

.align 2
trap_exit:
    li      a2, 0
    SEMIHOST_EXIT a2

# Build tiny RV64 fixtures used by hybrid smoke tests.
#
# Toolchain location comes from the repo-root config.env (loaded by
# `source ./setup.sh`, which exports HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN). Override on the
# command line with `make TOOLCHAIN=/path/to/toolchain ...` if you want
# to bypass the env var.

TOOLCHAIN ?= $(HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN)
ifeq ($(strip $(TOOLCHAIN)),)
$(error HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN is not set. Run `source ./setup.sh` from the repo root, or pass `TOOLCHAIN=/path/to/toolchain` on the command line)
endif
CC        := $(TOOLCHAIN)/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-gcc
LD        := $(TOOLCHAIN)/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-ld
OBJDUMP   := $(TOOLCHAIN)/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-objdump

# Runtime sources live at the repo root (runtime/) -- they are the
# user-facing andes-sim runtime; fixtures are just one consumer. The linker
# script moved with them (test.ld -> runtime/andes-sim.ld, same content).
RUNTIME_DIR := ../../runtime
LDSCRIPT    := $(RUNTIME_DIR)/andes-sim.ld
# Fixture-only helpers (csr ROI markers; NOT part of the portable runtime).
HELPERS_DIR := runtime

CFLAGS  := -march=rv64gc -mabi=lp64d -nostdlib -static -Wall
LDFLAGS := -T $(LDSCRIPT) -nostdlib -static

# All fixtures share andes-sim.ld (load base 0x00100000, andes_ae350 DRAM).
RT_FIXTURES := rt_all_gprs rt_abi_aliases rt_sign_bits rt_pc_jump \
               rt_long_roi rt_mem_loadstore rt_unaligned_lh \
               rt_shared_mem rt_csr_survival

# C-level fixtures: standard newlib stdio (printf, fputs, ...) linked
# through the shipped vplat runtime (libandes_sim_runtime.a) with the
# same two-flag command users type (-B build/runtime
# -specs=andes-sim.specs), so the suites regression-test the real
# artifact. stdio goes out the ATCUART100 UART2 and exit/file-io through
# the SimControl device at 0xe0080000, all of which both QEMU's
# andes_ae350 and vsim model. No semihosting and no libgloss anywhere:
# vplat_syscalls.o in the archive provides every stub newlib needs, so
# the same ELF runs on fast, cycle AND hybrid and a syscall inside the
# ROI works (it just adds its real cycles to the figure).
RT_C_FIXTURES    := rt_c_hello rt_c_printf rt_c_matmul rt_c_static_buf \
                    rt_c_no_trigger_exit rt_c_fcsr
RT_C_V_FIXTURES  := rt_c_v_regs rt_c_v_csrs rt_c_v_matmul rt_c_v_fill
RT_C_VPLAT_FIXTURES := vplat_hello vplat_exit41 vplat_file

RUNTIME_SRCS    := $(RUNTIME_DIR)/crt0.S $(RUNTIME_DIR)/trap.S \
                   $(RUNTIME_DIR)/handler.c
VPLAT_RT_DIR := ../../build/runtime
VPLAT_RT     := $(VPLAT_RT_DIR)/libandes_sim_runtime.a $(VPLAT_RT_DIR)/crt0.o \
                $(VPLAT_RT_DIR)/andes-sim.ld $(VPLAT_RT_DIR)/andes-sim.specs \
                $(VPLAT_RT_DIR)/include/andes_sim/roi.h
VPLAT_CFLAGS := -march=rv64gc -mabi=lp64d -O1 -Wall
# RVV-using fixtures need -march=rv64gcv; the runtime's rv64gc objects
# link cleanly into rv64gcv programs (ld unions the arch attributes).
# The crt0 already sets mstatus.VS to Initial, so V insns don't trap.
VPLAT_V_CFLAGS := -march=rv64gcv -mabi=lp64d -O1 -Wall

.PHONY: all clean dump

all: spin.elf icount_spin.elf handoff.elf handoff_exit.elf handoff_roundtrip.elf \
     $(RT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) $(RT_C_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) \
     $(RT_C_V_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) rt_c_v_matmul_free.elf \
     $(RT_C_VPLAT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf)

# Note: handoff.elf, handoff_exit.elf, spin.elf are referenced only by the
# EXCLUDE_FROM_ALL handoff_smoke.cpp target; they still build here for
# completeness. All targets share andes-sim.ld at 0x00100000.

spin.elf: spin.S $(LDSCRIPT)
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c spin.S -o spin.o
	$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) spin.o -o $@

# CSR-less spin for F5 plugin-icount e2e. Linked at 0x00100000 (andes-sim.ld)
# so andes_ae350's MROM at 0x80000000 stays clear when loaded via -bios.
icount_spin.elf: icount_spin.S $(LDSCRIPT)
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c icount_spin.S -o icount_spin.o
	$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) icount_spin.o -o $@

handoff.elf: handoff.S $(LDSCRIPT)
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c handoff.S -o handoff.o
	$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) handoff.o -o $@

handoff_exit.elf: handoff_exit.S $(LDSCRIPT)
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c handoff_exit.S -o handoff_exit.o
	$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) handoff_exit.o -o $@

handoff_roundtrip.elf: handoff_roundtrip.S $(LDSCRIPT) semihost_exit.inc
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c handoff_roundtrip.S -o handoff_roundtrip.o
	$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) handoff_roundtrip.o -o $@

$(RT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf): %.elf: %.S $(LDSCRIPT) semihost_exit.inc
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c $< -o $*.o
	$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) $*.o -o $@

# C-level fixtures: linked exactly like a user program (see VPLAT_RT
# above). rt_c_helpers.h rides -I$(HELPERS_DIR).
$(RT_C_FIXTURES:%=%.elf): %.elf: %.c $(VPLAT_RT) $(HELPERS_DIR)/rt_c_helpers.h
	$(CC) $(VPLAT_CFLAGS) -I$(HELPERS_DIR) \
	  -B $(VPLAT_RT_DIR) -specs=andes-sim.specs $< -o $@

# RVV-enabled fixtures: same link, different -march. Listed separately so
# changes to VPLAT_CFLAGS don't accidentally drop V.
$(RT_C_V_FIXTURES:%=%.elf): %.elf: %.c $(VPLAT_RT) $(HELPERS_DIR)/rt_c_helpers.h
	$(CC) $(VPLAT_V_CFLAGS) -I$(HELPERS_DIR) \
	  -B $(VPLAT_RT_DIR) -specs=andes-sim.specs $< -o $@

# vplat smoke fixtures (tests/vplat/): exercise the runtime's own
# features (exit code, file io) with no fixture helpers.
$(RT_C_VPLAT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf): %.elf: %.c $(VPLAT_RT)
	$(CC) $(VPLAT_CFLAGS) -B $(VPLAT_RT_DIR) -specs=andes-sim.specs $< -o $@

# One sub-make produces all five artifacts (grouped target, make >= 4.3).
$(VPLAT_RT) &: $(RUNTIME_SRCS) $(RUNTIME_DIR)/vplat_syscalls.c \
               $(RUNTIME_DIR)/andes-sim.ld $(RUNTIME_DIR)/andes-sim.specs \
               $(RUNTIME_DIR)/roi.h
	$(MAKE) -C $(RUNTIME_DIR)

# Markerless GEMM twin (gemm_modes.md F2). Explicit rule, NOT in
# RT_C_V_FIXTURES -- the pattern rule would look for a nonexistent
# rt_c_v_matmul_free.c. Same source, same link as the marked V fixtures,
# plus -DHYBRID_MARKERLESS (drops the ROI marker HINTs).
rt_c_v_matmul_free.elf: rt_c_v_matmul.c $(VPLAT_RT) $(HELPERS_DIR)/rt_c_helpers.h
	$(CC) $(VPLAT_V_CFLAGS) -DHYBRID_MARKERLESS -I$(HELPERS_DIR) \
	  -B $(VPLAT_RT_DIR) -specs=andes-sim.specs rt_c_v_matmul.c -o $@

dump: spin.elf handoff.elf handoff_exit.elf
	$(OBJDUMP) -d spin.elf
	$(OBJDUMP) -d handoff.elf
	$(OBJDUMP) -d handoff_exit.elf

clean:
	rm -f spin.o spin.elf handoff.o handoff.elf handoff_exit.o handoff_exit.elf \
	      handoff_roundtrip.o handoff_roundtrip.elf \
	      $(RT_FIXTURES:%=%.o) $(RT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) \
	      $(RT_C_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) $(RT_C_V_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) \
	      rt_c_v_matmul_free.elf $(RT_C_VPLAT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf)

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Run the hybrid e2e tests directly, bypassing the VSIM_ENABLE_HYBRID
# CTest gate. Drives tests/*.sh against pre-built artifacts in this
# workspace.
#
# Env overrides:
#   VSIM_QEMU    qemu-system-riscv64 (default: build/qemu/qemu-system-riscv64)
#   VSIM_PLUGIN  libhybrid_handoff.so (default: qemu_plugin/libhybrid_handoff.so)
#   VSIM_BIN     sim_<cpu> (default: first sim_* under verilator/build/)
#   FILTER       regex; only run tests whose name matches
#   MODE         marker | pc | both  (default: both) - drives TRIGGER_MODE
#                for round-trip fixtures. Negative drivers run once
#                regardless because they assert orchestrator failure
#                modes orthogonal to the trigger mechanism.
#   JOBS         parallel job slots (default: min($(nproc),
#                free(/dev/shm)/256MB)). Each Tier-2 slot uses a 128 MB
#                /dev/shm mmap and runs 2 processes (qemu1, vsim); the
#                headroom check leaves margin for that plus QEMU's own
#                scratch. Pass JOBS=1 for sequential semantics.
#   LOG_DIR      where per-test logs land (default: mktemp -d under /tmp)

set -euo pipefail

ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"
VSIM_DIR="$ROOT/verilator"
HARNESS="$ROOT/tests"
TEST_DIR="$ROOT/tests/fixtures"

VSIM_QEMU="${VSIM_QEMU:-$ROOT/build/qemu/qemu-system-riscv64}"
VSIM_PLUGIN="${VSIM_PLUGIN:-$ROOT/qemu_plugin/libhybrid_handoff.so}"
if [[ -z "${VSIM_BIN:-}" ]]; then
  # Default to the repo's canonical SINGLE-HART engine (the same one ./andes-sim
  # pins). The fixtures are single-hart programs: on a multicore build like
  # sim_ax45mpv_mp2 -- which sorts FIRST under verilator/build/ -- the
  # secondary hart runs crt0 from reset, writes SKIPPED to SimControl and
  # stops the sim before hart 0 drains, failing every C fixture. Fall back
  # to the first sim_* only when the canonical engine is not built.
  VSIM_BIN="$VSIM_DIR/build/sim_ax45mpv_premium"
  if [[ ! -x "$VSIM_BIN" ]]; then
    VSIM_BIN=$(ls "$VSIM_DIR"/build/sim_* 2>/dev/null | head -n1 || true)
  fi
fi

step() { printf '\033[1;34m==>\033[0m %s\n' "$*"; }
ok()   { printf '\033[1;32m[ok]\033[0m %s\n' "$*"; }
warn() { printf '\033[1;33m[skip]\033[0m %s\n' "$*"; }
fail() { printf '\033[1;31m[FAIL]\033[0m %s\n' "$*" >&2; }

require() {
  if [[ -z "$2" || ! -e "$2" ]]; then
    fail "$1 not found: $2"
    fail "build artifacts first: 'source ./setup.sh'"
    exit 1
  fi
}
require VSIM_QEMU   "$VSIM_QEMU"
require VSIM_PLUGIN "$VSIM_PLUGIN"
require VSIM_BIN    "$VSIM_BIN"

export VSIM_QEMU VSIM_PLUGIN VSIM_BIN

REQUIRED_ELFS=(
  handoff_roundtrip rt_pc_jump rt_sign_bits rt_abi_aliases rt_long_roi
  rt_all_gprs rt_mem_loadstore rt_unaligned_lh rt_csr_survival rt_shared_mem
  rt_c_hello rt_c_printf rt_c_matmul rt_c_fcsr rt_c_v_regs rt_c_v_csrs
  rt_c_v_matmul rt_c_v_fill
  # CSR-less spin loop; used by `./andes-sim run --mode icount` and the BBV-emit
  # / SimPoint stages.
  icount_spin
)
need_build=0
for f in "${REQUIRED_ELFS[@]}"; do
  [[ -e "$TEST_DIR/$f.elf" ]] || need_build=1
done
if (( need_build )); then
  step "building test ELFs in $TEST_DIR"
  make -C "$TEST_DIR" -j
fi

# Round-trip fixtures: name|fixture-env-prefix. All run on the unified
# e2e.sh harness (shared /dev/shm mmap). The TRIGGER_MODE env is
# injected per iteration based on $MODE. Negative drivers live in
# NEG_TESTS and run once regardless of mode.
RT_TESTS=(
  "handoff_roundtrip|FIXTURE=handoff_roundtrip"
  "rt_pc_jump|FIXTURE=rt_pc_jump"
  "rt_sign_bits|FIXTURE=rt_sign_bits"
  "rt_abi_aliases|FIXTURE=rt_abi_aliases"
  "rt_long_roi|FIXTURE=rt_long_roi"
  "rt_all_gprs|FIXTURE=rt_all_gprs"
  "rt_mem_loadstore|FIXTURE=rt_mem_loadstore"
  "rt_unaligned_lh|FIXTURE=rt_unaligned_lh"
  "rt_csr_survival|FIXTURE=rt_csr_survival"
  "rt_shared_mem|FIXTURE=rt_shared_mem"
  "rt_c_hello|FIXTURE=rt_c_hello"
  "rt_c_printf|FIXTURE=rt_c_printf"
  "rt_c_matmul|FIXTURE=rt_c_matmul TIMEOUT=120"
  "rt_c_fcsr|FIXTURE=rt_c_fcsr"
  "rt_c_v_regs|FIXTURE=rt_c_v_regs"
  "rt_c_v_csrs|FIXTURE=rt_c_v_csrs"
  "rt_c_v_matmul|FIXTURE=rt_c_v_matmul TIMEOUT=120"
  "rt_c_v_fill|FIXTURE=rt_c_v_fill"
  "rt_c_static_buf|FIXTURE=rt_c_static_buf"
)

NEG_TESTS=(
  "rt_corrupt_state|bash $HARNESS/drivers/rt_corrupt_state.sh"
)

MODE="${MODE:-both}"
case "$MODE" in
  marker|pc|both) ;;
  *) fail "MODE must be one of marker|pc|both (got: $MODE)"; exit 1 ;;
esac

default_jobs() {
  local n=1 shm_free shm_cap
  n=$(nproc 2>/dev/null || echo 1)
  if [[ -d /dev/shm ]]; then
    shm_free=$(df -m --output=avail /dev/shm 2>/dev/null | tail -n +2 | tr -d ' ')
    if [[ "$shm_free" =~ ^[0-9]+$ && "$shm_free" -gt 0 ]]; then
      shm_cap=$((shm_free / 256))
      (( shm_cap < n && shm_cap >= 1 )) && n=$shm_cap
    fi
  fi
  (( n < 1 )) && n=1
  printf '%d\n' "$n"
}
JOBS="${JOBS:-$(default_jobs)}"
[[ "$JOBS" =~ ^[0-9]+$ && "$JOBS" -ge 1 ]] \
  || { fail "JOBS must be a positive integer (got: $JOBS)"; exit 1; }

FILTER="${FILTER:-}"

LOG_DIR="${LOG_DIR:-$(mktemp -d -t e2e-XXXXXX)}"
mkdir -p "$LOG_DIR"
RESULTS_FILE="$LOG_DIR/results.tsv"
LOCK_FILE="$LOG_DIR/lock"
: > "$RESULTS_FILE"
: > "$LOCK_FILE"

# run_one MODE NAME CMD INDEX TOTAL
# Captures the test command's stdout+stderr into $LOG_DIR/$mode--$name.log,

5	# (128 MB). Works for both asm fixtures (handoff_roundtrip, rt_*) and
6	# C-level fixtures (rt_c_*). C fixtures require shared mmap so the
7	# stack/heap survives handoffs; asm fixtures don't need it but run
8	# fine with it.
9	#
10	# Env:
11	#   FIXTURE         REQUIRED. .elf name under tests/fixtures/ (no .elf suffix).
12	#   TRIGGER_MODE    marker | pc (default marker).

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Run the hybrid e2e tests directly, bypassing the VSIM_ENABLE_HYBRID
# CTest gate. Drives tests/*.sh against pre-built artifacts in this
# workspace.
#
# Env overrides:
#   VSIM_QEMU    qemu-system-riscv64 (default: build/qemu/qemu-system-riscv64)
#   VSIM_PLUGIN  libhybrid_handoff.so (default: qemu_plugin/libhybrid_handoff.so)
#   VSIM_BIN     sim_<cpu> (default: first sim_* under verilator/build/)
#   FILTER       regex; only run tests whose name matches
#   MODE         marker | pc | both  (default: both) - drives TRIGGER_MODE
#                for round-trip fixtures. Negative drivers run once
#                regardless because they assert orchestrator failure
#                modes orthogonal to the trigger mechanism.
#   JOBS         parallel job slots (default: min($(nproc),
#                free(/dev/shm)/256MB)). Each Tier-2 slot uses a 128 MB
#                /dev/shm mmap and runs 2 processes (qemu1, vsim); the
#                headroom check leaves margin for that plus QEMU's own
#                scratch. Pass JOBS=1 for sequential semantics.
#   LOG_DIR      where per-test logs land (default: mktemp -d under /tmp)

set -euo pipefail

ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"
VSIM_DIR="$ROOT/verilator"
HARNESS="$ROOT/tests"
TEST_DIR="$ROOT/tests/fixtures"

VSIM_QEMU="${VSIM_QEMU:-$ROOT/build/qemu/qemu-system-riscv64}"
VSIM_PLUGIN="${VSIM_PLUGIN:-$ROOT/qemu_plugin/libhybrid_handoff.so}"
if [[ -z "${VSIM_BIN:-}" ]]; then
  # Default to the repo's canonical SINGLE-HART engine (the same one ./andes-sim
  # pins). The fixtures are single-hart programs: on a multicore build like
  # sim_ax45mpv_mp2 -- which sorts FIRST under verilator/build/ -- the
  # secondary hart runs crt0 from reset, writes SKIPPED to SimControl and
  # stops the sim before hart 0 drains, failing every C fixture. Fall back
  # to the first sim_* only when the canonical engine is not built.
  VSIM_BIN="$VSIM_DIR/build/sim_ax45mpv_premium"
  if [[ ! -x "$VSIM_BIN" ]]; then
    VSIM_BIN=$(ls "$VSIM_DIR"/build/sim_* 2>/dev/null | head -n1 || true)
  fi
fi

step() { printf '\033[1;34m==>\033[0m %s\n' "$*"; }
ok()   { printf '\033[1;32m[ok]\033[0m %s\n' "$*"; }
warn() { printf '\033[1;33m[skip]\033[0m %s\n' "$*"; }
fail() { printf '\033[1;31m[FAIL]\033[0m %s\n' "$*" >&2; }

require() {
  if [[ -z "$2" || ! -e "$2" ]]; then
    fail "$1 not found: $2"
    fail "build artifacts first: 'source ./setup.sh'"
    exit 1
  fi
}

TEST_DIR="$ROOT/tests/fixtures"

VSIM_QEMU="${VSIM_QEMU:-$ROOT/build/qemu/qemu-system-riscv64}"
VSIM_PLUGIN="${VSIM_PLUGIN:-$ROOT/qemu_plugin/libhybrid_handoff.so}"
if [[ -z "${VSIM_BIN:-}" ]]; then
  # Default to the repo's canonical SINGLE-HART engine (the same one ./andes-sim
  # pins). The fixtures are single-hart programs: on a multicore build like
  # sim_ax45mpv_mp2 -- which sorts FIRST under verilator/build/ -- the
  # secondary hart runs crt0 from reset, writes SKIPPED to SimControl and
  # stops the sim before hart 0 drains, failing every C fixture. Fall back
  # to the first sim_* only when the canonical engine is not built.
  VSIM_BIN="$VSIM_DIR/build/sim_ax45mpv_premium"
  if [[ ! -x "$VSIM_BIN" ]]; then
    VSIM_BIN=$(ls "$VSIM_DIR"/build/sim_* 2>/dev/null | head -n1 || true)
  fi
fi

step() { printf '\033[1;34m==>\033[0m %s\n' "$*"; }
ok()   { printf '\033[1;32m[ok]\033[0m %s\n' "$*"; }
warn() { printf '\033[1;33m[skip]\033[0m %s\n' "$*"; }
fail() { printf '\033[1;31m[FAIL]\033[0m %s\n' "$*" >&2; }

require() {
  if [[ -z "$2" || ! -e "$2" ]]; then
    fail "$1 not found: $2"
    fail "build artifacts first: 'source ./setup.sh'"
    exit 1
  fi
}
require VSIM_QEMU   "$VSIM_QEMU"
require VSIM_PLUGIN "$VSIM_PLUGIN"
require VSIM_BIN    "$VSIM_BIN"

export VSIM_QEMU VSIM_PLUGIN VSIM_BIN

REQUIRED_ELFS=(
  handoff_roundtrip rt_pc_jump rt_sign_bits rt_abi_aliases rt_long_roi
  rt_all_gprs rt_mem_loadstore rt_unaligned_lh rt_csr_survival rt_shared_mem
  rt_priv_smode rt_priv_umode
  rt_c_hello rt_c_printf rt_c_matmul rt_c_fcsr rt_c_v_regs rt_c_v_csrs
  rt_c_v_matmul rt_c_v_fill
  # CSR-less spin loop; used by `./andes-sim run --mode icount` and the BBV-emit
  # / SimPoint stages.
  icount_spin
)
need_build=0
for f in "${REQUIRED_ELFS[@]}"; do
  [[ -e "$TEST_DIR/$f.elf" ]] || need_build=1
done
if (( need_build )); then
  step "building test ELFs in $TEST_DIR"
  make -C "$TEST_DIR" -j
fi

# Round-trip fixtures: name|fixture-env-prefix. All run on the unified
# e2e.sh harness (shared /dev/shm mmap). The TRIGGER_MODE env is
# injected per iteration based on $MODE. Negative drivers live in
# NEG_TESTS and run once regardless of mode.
RT_TESTS=(
  "handoff_roundtrip|FIXTURE=handoff_roundtrip"
  "rt_pc_jump|FIXTURE=rt_pc_jump"
  "rt_sign_bits|FIXTURE=rt_sign_bits"
  "rt_abi_aliases|FIXTURE=rt_abi_aliases"
  "rt_long_roi|FIXTURE=rt_long_roi"
  "rt_all_gprs|FIXTURE=rt_all_gprs"
  "rt_mem_loadstore|FIXTURE=rt_mem_loadstore"
  "rt_unaligned_lh|FIXTURE=rt_unaligned_lh"
  "rt_csr_survival|FIXTURE=rt_csr_survival"
  "rt_priv_smode|FIXTURE=rt_priv_smode CHECK_PRIV=1"
  "rt_priv_umode|FIXTURE=rt_priv_umode CHECK_PRIV=0"
  "rt_shared_mem|FIXTURE=rt_shared_mem"
  "rt_c_hello|FIXTURE=rt_c_hello"
  "rt_c_printf|FIXTURE=rt_c_printf"
  "rt_c_matmul|FIXTURE=rt_c_matmul TIMEOUT=120"
  "rt_c_fcsr|FIXTURE=rt_c_fcsr"
  "rt_c_v_regs|FIXTURE=rt_c_v_regs"
  "rt_c_v_csrs|FIXTURE=rt_c_v_csrs"
  "rt_c_v_matmul|FIXTURE=rt_c_v_matmul TIMEOUT=120"
  "rt_c_v_fill|FIXTURE=rt_c_v_fill"
  "rt_c_static_buf|FIXTURE=rt_c_static_buf"
)

NEG_TESTS=(
  "rt_corrupt_state|bash $HARNESS/drivers/rt_corrupt_state.sh"
)

MODE="${MODE:-both}"
case "$MODE" in
  marker|pc|both) ;;
  *) fail "MODE must be one of marker|pc|both (got: $MODE)"; exit 1 ;;
esac

default_jobs() {
  local n=1 shm_free shm_cap
  n=$(nproc 2>/dev/null || echo 1)
  if [[ -d /dev/shm ]]; then
    shm_free=$(df -m --output=avail /dev/shm 2>/dev/null | tail -n +2 | tr -d ' ')
    if [[ "$shm_free" =~ ^[0-9]+$ && "$shm_free" -gt 0 ]]; then
      shm_cap=$((shm_free / 256))
      (( shm_cap < n && shm_cap >= 1 )) && n=$shm_cap
    fi
  fi
  (( n < 1 )) && n=1
  printf '%d\n' "$n"
}
JOBS="${JOBS:-$(default_jobs)}"
[[ "$JOBS" =~ ^[0-9]+$ && "$JOBS" -ge 1 ]] \
  || { fail "JOBS must be a positive integer (got: $JOBS)"; exit 1; }

FILTER="${FILTER:-}"

LOG_DIR="${LOG_DIR:-$(mktemp -d -t e2e-XXXXXX)}"
mkdir -p "$LOG_DIR"
RESULTS_FILE="$LOG_DIR/results.tsv"
LOCK_FILE="$LOG_DIR/lock"
: > "$RESULTS_FILE"
: > "$LOCK_FILE"

# run_one MODE NAME CMD INDEX TOTAL
# Captures the test command's stdout+stderr into $LOG_DIR/$mode--$name.log,
# emits one atomic progress line, and appends a TSV row to $RESULTS_FILE
# (mode<TAB>name<TAB>status<TAB>rc<TAB>elapsed). flock on $LOCK_FILE
# serializes the progress write and the results-file append so concurrent
# children (introduced by the parallel-execution commit) cannot interleave
# their TTY writes or corrupt the tally file.
run_one() {
  local mode="$1" name="$2" cmd="$3" idx="$4" total="$5"
  local log="$LOG_DIR/$mode--$name.log"
  local start end elapsed status rc
  start=$(date +%s)
  set +e
  bash -c "$cmd" >"$log" 2>&1
  rc=$?
  set -e
  end=$(date +%s)
  elapsed=$((end - start))
  case $rc in
    0)  status=PASS ;;
    77) status=SKIP ;;
    *)  status=FAIL ;;
  esac
  (
    flock 9
    case "$status" in
      PASS) ok   "[$idx/$total] ${name}[${mode}] (${elapsed}s)" ;;
      SKIP) warn "[$idx/$total] ${name}[${mode}] (rc=77, ${elapsed}s)" ;;
      FAIL) fail "[$idx/$total] ${name}[${mode}] (rc=$rc, ${elapsed}s) -> $log" ;;
    esac
    printf '%s\t%s\t%s\t%d\t%d\n' \
      "$mode" "$name" "$status" "$rc" "$elapsed" >> "$RESULTS_FILE"
  ) 9>"$LOCK_FILE"
}

# Build the workplan: one entry per (mode, name, cmd) tuple. Order
# matters: marker-mode tests first, then pc-mode, then negatives (matching
# the original sequential layout so logs are streamed in the same order).
declare -a WORKPLAN=()
for tm in marker pc; do
  [[ "$MODE" != "both" && "$MODE" != "$tm" ]] && continue
  for entry in "${RT_TESTS[@]}"; do
    rt_name="${entry%%|*}"
    env_prefix="${entry#*|}"
    # B3: anchor the regex so FILTER=rt_csr does not silently also match
    # rt_csr_survival. Users who want a substring match pass '.*marker.*'.
    [[ -n "$FILTER" && ! "$rt_name" =~ ^$FILTER$ ]] && continue
    cmd="TRIGGER_MODE=$tm $env_prefix bash $HARNESS/e2e.sh"
    WORKPLAN+=("$tm|$rt_name|$cmd")
  done
done
for entry in "${NEG_TESTS[@]}"; do
  neg_name="${entry%%|*}"
  neg_cmd="${entry#*|}"
  [[ -n "$FILTER" && ! "$neg_name" =~ ^$FILTER$ ]] && continue
  WORKPLAN+=("neg|$neg_name|$neg_cmd")
done

TOTAL=${#WORKPLAN[@]}
step "logs: $LOG_DIR  jobs: $JOBS  mode: $MODE  tests: $TOTAL"

# FIFO-based bounded job pool. Each child reads one token from $SEM_FIFO
# before starting and writes one back on exit; only $JOBS tokens exist,
# so at most $JOBS children run concurrently. Opening the fifo in
# read-write mode (<>) means writes never block the parent. The fifo
# inode is unlinked immediately after fd 8 is bound -- the kernel keeps
# the pipe alive as long as fd 8 is open.
SEM_FIFO="$LOG_DIR/sem.fifo"
mkfifo "$SEM_FIFO"
exec 8<>"$SEM_FIFO"
rm -f "$SEM_FIFO"
for ((sem_i=0; sem_i<JOBS; sem_i++)); do
  printf '.\n' >&8
done

i=0
for w in "${WORKPLAN[@]}"; do
  i=$((i+1))
  w_mode="${w%%|*}"
  w_rest="${w#*|}"
  w_name="${w_rest%%|*}"
  w_cmd="${w_rest#*|}"
  read -r -u 8 _tok
  (
    run_one "$w_mode" "$w_name" "$w_cmd" "$i" "$TOTAL"
    printf '.\n' >&8
  ) &
done
wait
exec 8>&-

declare -A MODE_PASS=([marker]=0 [pc]=0 [neg]=0)
declare -A MODE_FAIL=([marker]=0 [pc]=0 [neg]=0)
declare -A MODE_SKIP=([marker]=0 [pc]=0 [neg]=0)
declare -a FAILED_NAMES=()
while IFS=$'\t' read -r r_mode r_name r_status _r_rc _r_el; do
  case "$r_status" in
    PASS) MODE_PASS[$r_mode]=$((MODE_PASS[$r_mode]+1)) ;;
    SKIP) MODE_SKIP[$r_mode]=$((MODE_SKIP[$r_mode]+1)) ;;
    FAIL) MODE_FAIL[$r_mode]=$((MODE_FAIL[$r_mode]+1));
          FAILED_NAMES+=("${r_name}[${r_mode}]") ;;
  esac
done < "$RESULTS_FILE"

# Stream failed-test logs in workplan order so the user sees a
# deterministic post-run failure dump.
for w in "${WORKPLAN[@]}"; do
  w_mode="${w%%|*}"
  w_rest="${w#*|}"
  w_name="${w_rest%%|*}"
  w_status=$(awk -F'\t' -v m="$w_mode" -v n="$w_name" \
                 '$1==m&&$2==n{print $3; exit}' "$RESULTS_FILE")
  if [[ "$w_status" == "FAIL" ]]; then
    echo
    echo "=== FAIL log: ${w_name}[${w_mode}] ==="
    cat "$LOG_DIR/$w_mode--$w_name.log"
  fi
done

echo
marker_p=${MODE_PASS[marker]} marker_f=${MODE_FAIL[marker]} marker_s=${MODE_SKIP[marker]}
pc_p=${MODE_PASS[pc]}   pc_f=${MODE_FAIL[pc]}   pc_s=${MODE_SKIP[pc]}
neg_p=${MODE_PASS[neg]} neg_f=${MODE_FAIL[neg]} neg_s=${MODE_SKIP[neg]}
total_pass=$((marker_p + pc_p + neg_p))
total_fail=$((marker_f + pc_f + neg_f))
total_skip=$((marker_s + pc_s + neg_s))
step "summary: marker ${marker_p}p/${marker_f}f/${marker_s}s  pc ${pc_p}p/${pc_f}f/${pc_s}s  neg ${neg_p}p/${neg_f}f/${neg_s}s  total ${total_pass} passed, ${total_fail} failed, ${total_skip} skipped"
if (( total_fail > 0 )); then
  fail "failures: ${FAILED_NAMES[*]}"
  exit 1
fi

98:**CSR restore split**: `ResumeDriver` writes only the CSRs that the vsim phase can touch: `mstatus`, `mtvec`, `mcycle`, `minstret`, and `fcsr` (frm + sticky fflags, gated on `HYBRID_FLAG_FP`; L20). The vsim phase is assumed trap-free and PMP-static; if a future workload needs traps or dynamic PMP inside the ROI, `ResumeDriver` must be extended.
116:`hybrid_state_v1` is the binary wire format exchanged between the QEMU plugin and vsim. It holds: 32 GPRs, 32 FPRs, fcsr, M-mode CSRs (mstatus, mepc, etc.), PMP (64 pmpaddr + 16 pmpcfg), and the V extension block (vstart, vtype, vl, vlenb, 32 vreg[], vxsat, vxrm, vcsr). `HYBRID_VLEN_BYTES_MAX=128` supports VLEN up to 1024 bits; the live width is the runtime `vlenb`, and a producer whose vlenb exceeds the ceiling refuses to drain instead of truncating (L11). Multi-byte fields are little-endian (native on RV64 + x86-64 host); the format is not endian-portable.

So the region you measure on vsim (between `enter_vsim` and `exit_vsim`)
MUST be:

- M-mode only (no S-mode, no U-mode)

- PMP-static (no memory-protection setup is carried in)
- No semihosting (exception: the vplat runtime's MMIO-backed
  stdio / exit / file io is supported inside the ROI, see L1)
- No atomics that cross the handoff boundary
- No MMIO other than the vplat device set, UART2 + SimControl/HTIF (see L9)

wrong or the run hangs. Each case is listed below.

- Note (2026-06-12 retitle): 128 MB is only the DEFAULT, not the limit.

- When it bites: heap, stack, or static data extends past the size in
  effect (default 128 MB), or the workload needs more than 2 GiB at all.
- What happens: there is no startup check that the ELF segments fit. vsim's

  `0x00000000..0x80000000`, QEMU rejects a larger `ram_size`, and the
  driver pre-caps at the same value -- no setting runs a > 2 GiB workload.
- Also unchecked: the V scratch region (4 KiB at GPA `0x00FF0000`) sits
  inside RAM and nothing verifies the ELF avoids it; a segment overlapping
  it is clobbered by the V sweep on hybrid V runs.

# priv_modes -- resolve L6: S/U-mode privilege across the handoff

Goal: a trap-free, paging-off ROI that sits in S- or U-mode at the
trigger boundary measures correctly. Today both drain sites hardcode
`priv = 3` and vsim never writes `dcsr.prv`, so `dret` always resumes
in M-mode (L6).

Input:  an ELF whose ROI runs in S- or U-mode (entered via `mret`
        before the ENTER marker, PMP opened in the M-mode preamble).
Output: `hybrid_state_v1::priv` carries the real privilege on both
        drains, vsim executes the ROI in that privilege, and the
        kernel-cycle figure is valid. `CHECK_PRIV=<0|1|3>` in

# Build the workplan: one entry per (mode, name, cmd) tuple. Order
# matters: marker-mode tests first, then pc-mode, then negatives (matching
# the original sequential layout so logs are streamed in the same order).
declare -a WORKPLAN=()
for tm in marker pc; do
  [[ "$MODE" != "both" && "$MODE" != "$tm" ]] && continue
  for entry in "${RT_TESTS[@]}"; do
    rt_name="${entry%%|*}"
    env_prefix="${entry#*|}"
    # B3: anchor the regex so FILTER=rt_csr does not silently also match
    # rt_csr_survival. Users who want a substring match pass '.*marker.*'.
    [[ -n "$FILTER" && ! "$rt_name" =~ ^$FILTER$ ]] && continue
    cmd="TRIGGER_MODE=$tm $env_prefix bash $HARNESS/e2e.sh"
    WORKPLAN+=("$tm|$rt_name|$cmd")
  done
done
for entry in "${NEG_TESTS[@]}"; do
  neg_name="${entry%%|*}"
  neg_cmd="${entry#*|}"
  [[ -n "$FILTER" && ! "$neg_name" =~ ^$FILTER$ ]] && continue
  WORKPLAN+=("neg|$neg_name|$neg_cmd")
done

TOTAL=${#WORKPLAN[@]}
step "logs: $LOG_DIR  jobs: $JOBS  mode: $MODE  tests: $TOTAL"

# FIFO-based bounded job pool. Each child reads one token from $SEM_FIFO
# before starting and writes one back on exit; only $JOBS tokens exist,
# so at most $JOBS children run concurrently. Opening the fifo in
# read-write mode (<>) means writes never block the parent. The fifo
# inode is unlinked immediately after fd 8 is bound -- the kernel keeps
# the pipe alive as long as fd 8 is open.
SEM_FIFO="$LOG_DIR/sem.fifo"
mkfifo "$SEM_FIFO"
exec 8<>"$SEM_FIFO"
rm -f "$SEM_FIFO"
for ((sem_i=0; sem_i<JOBS; sem_i++)); do
  printf '.\n' >&8
done

i=0
for w in "${WORKPLAN[@]}"; do
  i=$((i+1))
  w_mode="${w%%|*}"
  w_rest="${w#*|}"
  w_name="${w_rest%%|*}"
  w_cmd="${w_rest#*|}"
  read -r -u 8 _tok
  (
    run_one "$w_mode" "$w_name" "$w_cmd" "$i" "$TOTAL"
    printf '.\n' >&8
  ) &
done
wait
exec 8>&-

declare -A MODE_PASS=([marker]=0 [pc]=0 [neg]=0)
declare -A MODE_FAIL=([marker]=0 [pc]=0 [neg]=0)
declare -A MODE_SKIP=([marker]=0 [pc]=0 [neg]=0)
declare -a FAILED_NAMES=()
while IFS=$'\t' read -r r_mode r_name r_status _r_rc _r_el; do
  case "$r_status" in
    PASS) MODE_PASS[$r_mode]=$((MODE_PASS[$r_mode]+1)) ;;
    SKIP) MODE_SKIP[$r_mode]=$((MODE_SKIP[$r_mode]+1)) ;;
    FAIL) MODE_FAIL[$r_mode]=$((MODE_FAIL[$r_mode]+1));
          FAILED_NAMES+=("${r_name}[${r_mode}]") ;;
  esac
done < "$RESULTS_FILE"

# Stream failed-test logs in workplan order so the user sees a
# deterministic post-run failure dump.
for w in "${WORKPLAN[@]}"; do
  w_mode="${w%%|*}"
  w_rest="${w#*|}"
  w_name="${w_rest%%|*}"
  w_status=$(awk -F'\t' -v m="$w_mode" -v n="$w_name" \
                 '$1==m&&$2==n{print $3; exit}' "$RESULTS_FILE")
  if [[ "$w_status" == "FAIL" ]]; then
    echo
    echo "=== FAIL log: ${w_name}[${w_mode}] ==="
    cat "$LOG_DIR/$w_mode--$w_name.log"
  fi
done

echo
marker_p=${MODE_PASS[marker]} marker_f=${MODE_FAIL[marker]} marker_s=${MODE_SKIP[marker]}
pc_p=${MODE_PASS[pc]}   pc_f=${MODE_FAIL[pc]}   pc_s=${MODE_SKIP[pc]}

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Run the hybrid e2e tests directly, bypassing the VSIM_ENABLE_HYBRID
# CTest gate. Drives tests/*.sh against pre-built artifacts in this
# workspace.
#
# Env overrides:
#   VSIM_QEMU    qemu-system-riscv64 (default: build/qemu/qemu-system-riscv64)
#   VSIM_PLUGIN  libhybrid_handoff.so (default: qemu_plugin/libhybrid_handoff.so)
#   VSIM_BIN     sim_<cpu> (default: first sim_* under verilator/build/)
#   FILTER       regex; only run tests whose name matches
#   MODE         marker | pc | both  (default: both) - drives TRIGGER_MODE
#                for round-trip fixtures. Negative drivers run once
#                regardless because they assert orchestrator failure
#                modes orthogonal to the trigger mechanism.
#   JOBS         parallel job slots (default: min($(nproc),
#                free(/dev/shm)/256MB)). Each Tier-2 slot uses a 128 MB
#                /dev/shm mmap and runs 2 processes (qemu1, vsim); the
#                headroom check leaves margin for that plus QEMU's own
#                scratch. Pass JOBS=1 for sequential semantics.
#   LOG_DIR      where per-test logs land (default: mktemp -d under /tmp)

set -euo pipefail

ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"
VSIM_DIR="$ROOT/verilator"
HARNESS="$ROOT/tests"
TEST_DIR="$ROOT/tests/fixtures"

VSIM_QEMU="${VSIM_QEMU:-$ROOT/build/qemu/qemu-system-riscv64}"
VSIM_PLUGIN="${VSIM_PLUGIN:-$ROOT/qemu_plugin/libhybrid_handoff.so}"
if [[ -z "${VSIM_BIN:-}" ]]; then
  # Default to the repo's canonical SINGLE-HART engine (the same one ./andes-sim
  # pins). The fixtures are single-hart programs: on a multicore build like
  # sim_ax45mpv_mp2 -- which sorts FIRST under verilator/build/ -- the
  # secondary hart runs crt0 from reset, writes SKIPPED to SimControl and
  # stops the sim before hart 0 drains, failing every C fixture. Fall back
  # to the first sim_* only when the canonical engine is not built.
  VSIM_BIN="$VSIM_DIR/build/sim_ax45mpv_premium"
  if [[ ! -x "$VSIM_BIN" ]]; then
    VSIM_BIN=$(ls "$VSIM_DIR"/build/sim_* 2>/dev/null | head -n1 || true)
  fi
fi

step() { printf '\033[1;34m==>\033[0m %s\n' "$*"; }
ok()   { printf '\033[1;32m[ok]\033[0m %s\n' "$*"; }
warn() { printf '\033[1;33m[skip]\033[0m %s\n' "$*"; }
fail() { printf '\033[1;31m[FAIL]\033[0m %s\n' "$*" >&2; }

require() {
  if [[ -z "$2" || ! -e "$2" ]]; then
    fail "$1 not found: $2"
    fail "build artifacts first: 'source ./setup.sh'"
    exit 1
  fi
}
require VSIM_QEMU   "$VSIM_QEMU"
require VSIM_PLUGIN "$VSIM_PLUGIN"
require VSIM_BIN    "$VSIM_BIN"

export VSIM_QEMU VSIM_PLUGIN VSIM_BIN

REQUIRED_ELFS=(
  handoff_roundtrip rt_pc_jump rt_sign_bits rt_abi_aliases rt_long_roi
  rt_all_gprs rt_mem_loadstore rt_unaligned_lh rt_csr_survival rt_shared_mem
  rt_priv_smode rt_priv_umode
  rt_c_hello rt_c_printf rt_c_matmul rt_c_fcsr rt_c_v_regs rt_c_v_csrs
  rt_c_v_matmul rt_c_v_fill
  # CSR-less spin loop; used by `./andes-sim run --mode icount` and the BBV-emit
  # / SimPoint stages.
  icount_spin
)
need_build=0
for f in "${REQUIRED_ELFS[@]}"; do
  [[ -e "$TEST_DIR/$f.elf" ]] || need_build=1
done
if (( need_build )); then
  step "building test ELFs in $TEST_DIR"
  make -C "$TEST_DIR" -j
fi

# Round-trip fixtures: name|fixture-env-prefix. All run on the unified
# e2e.sh harness (shared /dev/shm mmap). The TRIGGER_MODE env is
# injected per iteration based on $MODE. Negative drivers live in
# NEG_TESTS and run once regardless of mode.
RT_TESTS=(
  "handoff_roundtrip|FIXTURE=handoff_roundtrip"
  "rt_pc_jump|FIXTURE=rt_pc_jump"
  "rt_sign_bits|FIXTURE=rt_sign_bits"
  "rt_abi_aliases|FIXTURE=rt_abi_aliases"
  "rt_long_roi|FIXTURE=rt_long_roi"
  "rt_all_gprs|FIXTURE=rt_all_gprs"
  "rt_mem_loadstore|FIXTURE=rt_mem_loadstore"
  "rt_unaligned_lh|FIXTURE=rt_unaligned_lh"
  "rt_csr_survival|FIXTURE=rt_csr_survival"
  "rt_shared_mem|FIXTURE=rt_shared_mem"
  "rt_c_hello|FIXTURE=rt_c_hello"
  "rt_c_printf|FIXTURE=rt_c_printf"
  "rt_c_matmul|FIXTURE=rt_c_matmul TIMEOUT=120"
  "rt_c_fcsr|FIXTURE=rt_c_fcsr"
  "rt_c_v_regs|FIXTURE=rt_c_v_regs"
  "rt_c_v_csrs|FIXTURE=rt_c_v_csrs"
  "rt_c_v_matmul|FIXTURE=rt_c_v_matmul TIMEOUT=120"
  "rt_c_v_fill|FIXTURE=rt_c_v_fill"
  "rt_c_static_buf|FIXTURE=rt_c_static_buf"
)

NEG_TESTS=(
  "rt_corrupt_state|bash $HARNESS/drivers/rt_corrupt_state.sh"
)

MODE="${MODE:-both}"
case "$MODE" in
  marker|pc|both) ;;
  *) fail "MODE must be one of marker|pc|both (got: $MODE)"; exit 1 ;;
esac

default_jobs() {
  local n=1 shm_free shm_cap
  n=$(nproc 2>/dev/null || echo 1)
  if [[ -d /dev/shm ]]; then
    shm_free=$(df -m --output=avail /dev/shm 2>/dev/null | tail -n +2 | tr -d ' ')
    if [[ "$shm_free" =~ ^[0-9]+$ && "$shm_free" -gt 0 ]]; then
      shm_cap=$((shm_free / 256))
      (( shm_cap < n && shm_cap >= 1 )) && n=$shm_cap
    fi
  fi
  (( n < 1 )) && n=1
  printf '%d\n' "$n"
}
JOBS="${JOBS:-$(default_jobs)}"
[[ "$JOBS" =~ ^[0-9]+$ && "$JOBS" -ge 1 ]] \
  || { fail "JOBS must be a positive integer (got: $JOBS)"; exit 1; }

FILTER="${FILTER:-}"

LOG_DIR="${LOG_DIR:-$(mktemp -d -t e2e-XXXXXX)}"
mkdir -p "$LOG_DIR"
RESULTS_FILE="$LOG_DIR/results.tsv"
LOCK_FILE="$LOG_DIR/lock"
: > "$RESULTS_FILE"
: > "$LOCK_FILE"

# run_one MODE NAME CMD INDEX TOTAL
# Captures the test command's stdout+stderr into $LOG_DIR/$mode--$name.log,
# emits one atomic progress line, and appends a TSV row to $RESULTS_FILE
# (mode<TAB>name<TAB>status<TAB>rc<TAB>elapsed). flock on $LOCK_FILE
# serializes the progress write and the results-file append so concurrent
# children (introduced by the parallel-execution commit) cannot interleave
# their TTY writes or corrupt the tally file.
run_one() {
  local mode="$1" name="$2" cmd="$3" idx="$4" total="$5"
  local log="$LOG_DIR/$mode--$name.log"
  local start end elapsed status rc
  start=$(date +%s)
  set +e
  bash -c "$cmd" >"$log" 2>&1
  rc=$?
  set -e
  end=$(date +%s)
  elapsed=$((end - start))
  case $rc in
    0)  status=PASS ;;
    77) status=SKIP ;;
    *)  status=FAIL ;;
  esac
  (
    flock 9
    case "$status" in
      PASS) ok   "[$idx/$total] ${name}[${mode}] (${elapsed}s)" ;;
      SKIP) warn "[$idx/$total] ${name}[${mode}] (rc=77, ${elapsed}s)" ;;
      FAIL) fail "[$idx/$total] ${name}[${mode}] (rc=$rc, ${elapsed}s) -> $log" ;;
    esac
    printf '%s\t%s\t%s\t%d\t%d\n' \
      "$mode" "$name" "$status" "$rc" "$elapsed" >> "$RESULTS_FILE"
  ) 9>"$LOCK_FILE"
}

# Build the workplan: one entry per (mode, name, cmd) tuple. Order
# matters: marker-mode tests first, then pc-mode, then negatives (matching
# the original sequential layout so logs are streamed in the same order).
declare -a WORKPLAN=()
for tm in marker pc; do
  [[ "$MODE" != "both" && "$MODE" != "$tm" ]] && continue
  for entry in "${RT_TESTS[@]}"; do
    rt_name="${entry%%|*}"
    env_prefix="${entry#*|}"
    # B3: anchor the regex so FILTER=rt_csr does not silently also match
    # rt_csr_survival. Users who want a substring match pass '.*marker.*'.
    [[ -n "$FILTER" && ! "$rt_name" =~ ^$FILTER$ ]] && continue
    cmd="TRIGGER_MODE=$tm $env_prefix bash $HARNESS/e2e.sh"
    WORKPLAN+=("$tm|$rt_name|$cmd")
  done
done
for entry in "${NEG_TESTS[@]}"; do
  neg_name="${entry%%|*}"
  neg_cmd="${entry#*|}"
  [[ -n "$FILTER" && ! "$neg_name" =~ ^$FILTER$ ]] && continue
  WORKPLAN+=("neg|$neg_name|$neg_cmd")
done

TOTAL=${#WORKPLAN[@]}
step "logs: $LOG_DIR  jobs: $JOBS  mode: $MODE  tests: $TOTAL"

# FIFO-based bounded job pool. Each child reads one token from $SEM_FIFO
# before starting and writes one back on exit; only $JOBS tokens exist,
# so at most $JOBS children run concurrently. Opening the fifo in
# read-write mode (<>) means writes never block the parent. The fifo
# inode is unlinked immediately after fd 8 is bound -- the kernel keeps
# the pipe alive as long as fd 8 is open.
SEM_FIFO="$LOG_DIR/sem.fifo"
mkfifo "$SEM_FIFO"
exec 8<>"$SEM_FIFO"
rm -f "$SEM_FIFO"
for ((sem_i=0; sem_i<JOBS; sem_i++)); do
  printf '.\n' >&8
done

i=0
for w in "${WORKPLAN[@]}"; do
  i=$((i+1))
  w_mode="${w%%|*}"
  w_rest="${w#*|}"
  w_name="${w_rest%%|*}"
  w_cmd="${w_rest#*|}"
  read -r -u 8 _tok
  (
    run_one "$w_mode" "$w_name" "$w_cmd" "$i" "$TOTAL"
    printf '.\n' >&8
  ) &
done
wait
exec 8>&-

declare -A MODE_PASS=([marker]=0 [pc]=0 [neg]=0)
declare -A MODE_FAIL=([marker]=0 [pc]=0 [neg]=0)
declare -A MODE_SKIP=([marker]=0 [pc]=0 [neg]=0)
declare -a FAILED_NAMES=()
while IFS=$'\t' read -r r_mode r_name r_status _r_rc _r_el; do
  case "$r_status" in
    PASS) MODE_PASS[$r_mode]=$((MODE_PASS[$r_mode]+1)) ;;
    SKIP) MODE_SKIP[$r_mode]=$((MODE_SKIP[$r_mode]+1)) ;;
    FAIL) MODE_FAIL[$r_mode]=$((MODE_FAIL[$r_mode]+1));
          FAILED_NAMES+=("${r_name}[${r_mode}]") ;;
  esac
done < "$RESULTS_FILE"

# Stream failed-test logs in workplan order so the user sees a
# deterministic post-run failure dump.
for w in "${WORKPLAN[@]}"; do
  w_mode="${w%%|*}"
  w_rest="${w#*|}"
  w_name="${w_rest%%|*}"
  w_status=$(awk -F'\t' -v m="$w_mode" -v n="$w_name" \
                 '$1==m&&$2==n{print $3; exit}' "$RESULTS_FILE")
  if [[ "$w_status" == "FAIL" ]]; then
    echo
    echo "=== FAIL log: ${w_name}[${w_mode}] ==="
    cat "$LOG_DIR/$w_mode--$w_name.log"
  fi
done

echo
marker_p=${MODE_PASS[marker]} marker_f=${MODE_FAIL[marker]} marker_s=${MODE_SKIP[marker]}
pc_p=${MODE_PASS[pc]}   pc_f=${MODE_FAIL[pc]}   pc_s=${MODE_SKIP[pc]}
neg_p=${MODE_PASS[neg]} neg_f=${MODE_FAIL[neg]} neg_s=${MODE_SKIP[neg]}
total_pass=$((marker_p + pc_p + neg_p))
total_fail=$((marker_f + pc_f + neg_f))
total_skip=$((marker_s + pc_s + neg_s))
step "summary: marker ${marker_p}p/${marker_f}f/${marker_s}s  pc ${pc_p}p/${pc_f}f/${pc_s}s  neg ${neg_p}p/${neg_f}f/${neg_s}s  total ${total_pass} passed, ${total_fail} failed, ${total_skip} skipped"
if (( total_fail > 0 )); then
  fail "failures: ${FAILED_NAMES[*]}"
  exit 1
fi

vsim's exit-trigger drain is NOT insn-precise: between the exit marker/pc
retiring and the DMI haltreq taking effect, the AX45MPV core retires a
variable 0-3 more instructions. The drained pc (DPC) and any GPRs those
slack insns touch reflect the later sample point. This is inherent to the
DMI halt path, not a bug; the mcycle figure already includes the slack.

the drained pc, not to trigger+1. The QEMU plugin's oracle mode does this
via `exit_marker=1|exit_pc=0x... , drain_pc=<vsim drained pc>` (arm at the
boundary, drain at the first post-arm hit of drain_pc). See verify_oracle.md

content.text:
L6 is resolved: the handoff now transports the real privilege level, and S/U-mode ROIs measure correctly on the cycle-accurate engine. Full e2e suite: **43/43 pass** (was 39 tests; 4 new privilege tests added).

**What changed** (roadmap: `priv_modes.md`; 5 submodule commits + 2 parent commits on `code-review`):

- **QEMU plugin** drains the gdbstub `priv` virtual register instead of hardcoding M-mode (`hybrid_handoff.c`).
- **ResumeDriver** read-modify-writes `dcsr.prv` before `dret` so the hart resumes in the drained privilege, rejects the reserved value 2, and for S/U states first mirrors the producer's PMP block (64 `pmpaddr` + 8 even `pmpcfg`) — with PMP implemented and no matching entry, every S/U access faults, so an S/U ROI cannot even fetch without it. This moves **L2 to partial**.
- **StateDrain** reads `dcsr.prv` back at the exit halt, so the drained file records the privilege the ROI actually ran in; `--verify` compares it against the QEMU oracle.
- **e2e**: `rt_priv_smode` / `rt_priv_umode` fixtures (M-mode preamble opens PMP, `mret` into the ROI, trap-based exit) with a `CHECK_PRIV` harness assert, both trigger modes.

**Two findings you should know about:**

1. **The default engine cannot run S/U code.** The `ax45mpv_premium` RTL is built with `NDS_NUM_PRIVILEGE_LEVELS=1`, so the hardware WARL-pins `dcsr.prv` to M. The resume now reads the field back and **aborts loudly** ("engine does not implement privilege level 1 ... pick an S/U-capable engine") instead of silently measuring in the wrong mode. The priv tests run on `ax66_makatau` (3 privilege levels, 16 PMP entries) paired with QEMU `-cpu andes-ax66` — it was already part of the standard build.
2. **The ax66 tests needed a scheduling fix.** Two 32-thread ax66 processes inside the JOBS=8 parallel pool starved the whole box and timed out unrelated tests. `run_e2e.sh` now runs heavyweight entries in a serial phase after the pool drains; each priv test takes ~70s there, and the previously flaky tests went back to green.

Also, the halt-slack is core-dependent: on ax66 the exit halt retired past 4 insns after the trigger (the fixture's `ecall` fired before the halt landed, trapping to M). The fixtures pad 16 nops after the EXIT marker; I updated the halt-slack memory note.

**Residual envelope (documented in the notebook/USER_GUIDE):** the ROI must stay in one privilege (no traps or `xRET` inside), paging stays off (L3), and S-mode CSRs (`stvec`, `sscratch`, ...) are still not transported — an S-mode ROI that reads them sees vsim reset values.

One pre-existing issue I found but left alone (scope): `icount_trigger.test.cpp` and `measure_start_snapshot.test.cpp` don't compile at submodule HEAD — they call a two-argument `on_retire(pc, lambda)` that `handoff_controller.hpp` no longer has (same rot class as the relink-audit repairs in 96f9de5). Say the word if you want them repaired.

===== cell 3 (markdown) =====
## The core rule: the vsim measurement window (ROI) is very narrow

This is the single most important limitation. Everything in Tier 1 is a
consequence of it.

When execution hands off to vsim, the resume step writes back only a small
part of the CPU state. Read `resume_driver.hpp`: it restores GPRs,
FPRs, the V registers, PC, and only five CSRs - `mstatus`, `mtvec`,
`mcycle`, `minstret`, and (since L20 was resolved on 2026-06-12) `fcsr`.
It does NOT write `satp`, `mepc`, `mcause`, `mtval`,
`mscratch`, `medeleg`, `mideleg`, `mip`, `mie`, or any PMP register.

The cell below prints the complete CSR list the resume driver knows. Note
what is missing: no `satp`, no `mepc`/`mcause`/`mtval`, no PMP.

35:  static constexpr uint16_t kCsrFcsr     = 0x003;

37:  static constexpr uint16_t kCsrMtvec    = 0x305;

42:  static constexpr uint16_t kCsrVxrm     = 0x00A;
